name: Bamboo India
tagline: Pune brand replacing everyday plastic items with bamboo
excerpt: Bamboo India, maker of bamboo toothbrushes and other plastic alternatives, closed a ₹50 lakh deal on Shark Tank India Season 1, Episode 16.
content:
Bamboo India makes bamboo versions of everyday plastic products, starting with the toothbrush. A husband-and-wife team pitched it in the 16th episode of Shark Tank India, aired on 10 January 2022.

SET India's own clip describes a ₹50 lakh deal being fixed with the sharks. The stake, any debt component and the investing sharks were not confirmed by an outlet we rely on, so we leave them out.

We could not find a filing-based report of the company's revenue or funding since the show.

shark_tank.pitch_summary: A couple pitched bamboo toothbrushes and other plastic substitutes and closed a ₹50 lakh deal.

sources.label: SET India (official YouTube): 'Bamboo India' fixes a ₹50 lakh deal with the sharks, 20 Mar 2023
SET India (official YouTube): Shark Tank India Ep 16, full episode, 10 January 2022

deal_closed.detail: We found no filing-based report confirming the investment.

pitch_video.title: Final Offer | 'Bamboo India' ने Sharks के साथ Fix की 50 Lakhs की Deal! | Shark Tank India

faq.q: Did Bamboo India get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Yes. SET India's clip shows a ₹50 lakh deal agreed in Season 1, Episode 16.

lessons: Our analysis: a single hero product (the toothbrush) gave a broad sustainability mission a simple entry point.
notes: BELOW PUBLISHING BAR (no sourced ask). Blogs and Wikipedia give ask ₹80 lakh for 4% and deal ₹50 lakh for 3.5% plus ₹30 lakh debt from Ashneer Grover and Anupam Mittal; founders Yogesh and Ashwini Shinde, Pune. None confirmed by a credible outlet. Inc42 Datalabs entity 'Bamboo India Private Limited' shows near-zero figures, likely not the trading entity, so not used.
